---
title: "Analysing Ecological Variables within the Habitat"
author: "Kaytlin Edwards"
date: "2026-11-20"
output: html_document
---

This section looks at environmental conditions around Peak Island, Queensland, where seven female flatback turtles (*Natator depressus*) were tracked during the 2024 nesting season. Environmental data from Google Earth Engine were used to examine the areas visited by turtles during their inter-nesting periods. Benthic habitats and geomorphic zones from the Allen Coral Atlas were explored to identify habitat types, while mangrove coverage and Sentinel-2 turbidity data were examined to better understand the surrounding coastal environment and differences in water conditions across the study area.

## 3.1 Load Required Packages.

```{r packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(ggridges)
```

## 3.2 Import Environmental Data

Environmental raster datasets were exported from Google Earth Engine for analysis. The datasets include benthic habitat classifications, geomorphic zones, mangrove extent and a turbidity proxy.

```{r import-environmental-data}
benthic <- rast(here("data", "Ecosystem_Data",
                    "PeakIsland_Benthic_Habitats.tif"))

geomorphic <- rast(here("data", "Ecosystem_Data",
                       "PeakIsland_Geomorphic_Zones.tif"))

mangroves <- rast(here("data", "Ecosystem_Data",
                      "PeakIsland_Mangrovepresence_2023.tif"))

turbidity <- rast(here("data", "Ecosystem_Data",
                     "PeakIsland_Turbidity_Proxy_2024.tif"))
```

## 3.3 Benthic Habitat & Geomorphic Zones

### 3.3.1 Benthic Habitat Cleaning and Classification

```{r benthic-classifications}
# Define Allen Coral Atlas benthic habitat classifications
benthic_classes <- tibble(
  benthic_code = c(0, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 18),
  benthic_habitat = c(
    "Unmapped",
    "Sand",
    "Rubble",
    "Rock",
    "Seagrass",
    "Coral/Algae",
    "Microalgal Mats"
  )
)

# Display classification table
benthic_classes
```

### 3.3.2 Geomorphic Zone Classification

```{r geomorphic-classifications}
# Define Allen Coral Atlas geomorphic zone classifications
geomorphic_classes <- tibble(
  geomorphic_code = c(0, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15,
                     16, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25),
  geomorphic_zone = c(
    "Unmapped",
    "Shallow Lagoon",
    "Deep Lagoon",
    "Inner Reef Flat",
    "Outer Reef Flat",
    "Reef Crest",
    "Terrestrial Reef Flat",
    "Sheltered Reef Slope",
    "Reef Slope",
    "Plateau",
    "Back Reef Slope",
    "Patch Reef"
  )
)

# Display geomorphic classification table
geomorphic_classes
```

### 3.3.3 Summarise Habitat Classifications

```{r summarise-benthic}

# Import cleaned inter-nesting tracking observations
turtle_internesting <- readr::read_csv(
  here::here("outputs", "Turtle_Internesting_Cleaned.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Create spatial points from inter-nesting observations
turtle_habitat_points <- terra::vect(
  turtle_internesting,
  geom = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)

# Extract benthic habitat values
benthic_values <- terra::extract(
  benthic,
  terra::project(turtle_habitat_points, terra::crs(benthic))
)

# Extract geomorphic zone values
geomorphic_values <- terra::extract(
  geomorphic,
  terra::project(turtle_habitat_points, terra::crs(geomorphic))
)

# Create habitat dataset using the same inter-nesting observations
turtle_habitat <- turtle_internesting %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    benthic = benthic_values[[2]],
    geomorphic = geomorphic_values[[2]]
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    benthic_classes,
    by = c("benthic" = "benthic_code")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    geomorphic_classes,
    by = c("geomorphic" = "geomorphic_code")
  )

# Summarise benthic classifications
benthic_summary <- turtle_habitat %>%
  dplyr::count(benthic_habitat, name = "observations") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    percentage = round(observations / sum(observations) * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(observations))

benthic_summary

# Summarise geomorphic classifications
geomorphic_summary <- turtle_habitat %>%
  dplyr::count(geomorphic_zone, name = "observations") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    percentage = round(observations / sum(observations) * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(observations))

geomorphic_summary
```

After comparing the benthic and geomorphic classifications with turtle tracking locations, approximately 95.8% of observations fell within unmapped areas. With so few locations assigned to a habitat type, there isn't enough information to make meaningful comparisons. Because of this, benthic and geomorphic habitat analysis will not be analysed any further.

## 3.4 Mangroves

### 3.4.1 Prepare Mangrove Habitat Buffers

```{r mangrove-buffers}
# Identify pixels containing mangroves
mangrove_presence <- ifel(mangroves > 0, 1, NA)

# Convert mangrove pixels to polygons
mangrove_polygons <- as.polygons(
  mangrove_presence,
  dissolve = TRUE,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# Reproject to a coordinate system measured in metres
mangrove_polygons <- project(
  mangrove_polygons,
  "EPSG:7856"
)

# Create buffers extending beyond mangrove habitat
mangrove_buffer_100m <- terra::buffer(mangrove_polygons, width = 100)
mangrove_buffer_500m <- terra::buffer(mangrove_polygons, width = 500)
mangrove_buffer_1km <- terra::buffer(mangrove_polygons, width = 1000)
```

### 3.4.2 Visualise Mangrove Habitat and Buffers

```{r check-mangrove-buffer, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
plot(
  mangrove_buffer_100m,
  col = "lightblue",
  border = NA,
  main = "Mangrove Habitat and 100 m Buffer"
)

plot(
  mangrove_polygons,
  col = "darkgreen",
  border = NA,
  add = TRUE
)
```

### 3.4.4 Calculate Distance to Nearest Mangrove Habitat

```{r mangrove-buffer-summary}
# Calculate distance to nearest mangrove habitat (metres)
mangrove_distance_m <- terra::distance(
  turtle_points_mangrove,
  mangrove_polygons
)

# Group turtle observations by distance from mangroves
mangrove_buffer_summary <- tibble(
  distance_m = as.numeric(mangrove_distance_m)
) %>%
  mutate(
    buffer = case_when(
      is.na(distance_m) ~ NA_character_,
      distance_m <= 100 ~ "0–100 m",
      distance_m <= 500 ~ "100–500 m",
      distance_m <= 1000 ~ "500 m–1 km",
      TRUE ~ ">1 km"
    ),
    buffer = factor(
      buffer,
      levels = c(
        "0–100 m",
        "100–500 m",
        "500 m–1 km",
        ">1 km"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  count(buffer, name = "observations", .drop = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = round(observations / sum(observations) * 100, 1)
  )

# Display summary table
mangrove_buffer_summary
```

### 3.4.5 Mangrove Proximity by Turtle

Including only inter-nesting observations.

```{r mangrove-proximity-by-turtle}
# Summarise mangrove proximity for each turtle
mangrove_by_turtle <- turtle_internesting %>%
  mutate(
    distance_m = as.numeric(mangrove_distance_m)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Turtleid) %>%
  summarise(
    total_observations = n(),
    within_1km = sum(distance_m <= 1000, na.rm = TRUE),
    percentage = round(within_1km / total_observations * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(within_1km))

mangrove_by_turtle

# Group observations by distance from mangroves
turtle_mangrove_distances <- turtle_internesting %>%
  mutate(
    distance_m = as.numeric(mangrove_distance_m),
    buffer = case_when(
      is.na(distance_m) ~ NA_character_,
      distance_m <= 100 ~ "0–100 m",
      distance_m <= 500 ~ "100–500 m",
      distance_m <= 1000 ~ "500 m–1 km",
      TRUE ~ ">1 km"
    ),
    buffer = factor(
      buffer,
      levels = c(
        "0–100 m",
        "100–500 m",
        "500 m–1 km",
        ">1 km"
      )
    )
  )
```

```{r mangrove-observations-by-turtle, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}

# Count observations within 1 km for each turtle
mangrove_turtle_plot <- turtle_mangrove_distances %>%
  filter(distance_m <= 1000) %>%
  count(Turtleid, buffer, name = "observations")

# Include all seven turtles on the x-axis
all_turtle_ids <- sort(unique(turtle_internesting$Turtleid))

# Calculate total counts and percentages for bar labels
mangrove_labels <- turtle_mangrove_distances %>%
  group_by(Turtleid) %>%
  summarise(
    total_observations = n(),
    within_1km = sum(distance_m <= 1000, na.rm = TRUE),
    percentage = round(within_1km / total_observations * 100, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  mangrove_turtle_plot,
  aes(
    x = factor(Turtleid, levels = all_turtle_ids),
    y = observations,
    fill = buffer
  )
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    data = mangrove_labels,
    aes(
      x = factor(Turtleid, levels = all_turtle_ids),
      y = within_1km,
      label = paste0(percentage, "%")
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "0–100 m" = "#326B49",
      "100–500 m" = "#72A77A",
      "500 m–1 km" = "#B9D8B0"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Turtle Observations Within 1 km of Mangroves",
    x = "Turtle ID",
    y = "Number of Tracking Points",
    fill = "Distance from Mangroves"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

```


## 3.5 Turbidity

### 3.5.1 Examine Turbidity Distribution
```{r turbidity-distribution}
turbidity_percentiles <- terra::global(
  turbidity,
  fun = function(x, ...) {
    quantile(
      x[is.finite(x)],
      probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95, 0.99, 1)
    )
  }
)

turbidity_percentiles
```

### 3.5.2 Visualise Turbidity Distribution

```{r turbidity-visualisation, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
# Display turbidity using the 99th percentile colour limit
plot(
  turbidity,
  main = "Water Turbidity Proxy (2024)",
  col = hcl.colors(100, "Viridis"),
  range = c(0, 0.1227)
)
```

## 3.5.3 Overlay Turtle Tracking Locations on Turbidity

Satellite-tracking locations were overlaid on the 2024 turbidity proxy to examine the relationship between turtle movements and water turbidity.

```{r turtle-turbidity-overlay, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
# Import tracking observations outside the nesting-site buffer
turtle_internesting <- readr::read_csv(
  here::here("data", "Turtle_Internesting_Cleaned.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)


# Convert inter-nesting observations to spatial points
turtle_points <- terra::vect(
  turtle_internesting,
  geom = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)

# Match the coordinate system of the turbidity raster
turtle_points <- terra::project(
  turtle_points,
  terra::crs(turbidity)
)

# Plot turbidity
plot(
  turbidity,
  main = "Flatback Turtle Locations and Water Turbidity (2024)",
  col = hcl.colors(100, "Viridis"),
  range = c(0, 0.1227)

# Overlay turtle tracking locations
points(
  turtle_points,
  pch = 16,
  col = "red",
  cex = 0.4
)
```

## 3.5.4 Extract Turbidity Values at Turtle Locations

```{r extract-turbidity}
# Extract turbidity values at inter-nesting turtle locations
turtle_turbidity <- terra::extract(
  turbidity,
  turtle_points
)

# Combine extracted turbidity with turtle observations
turtle_turbidity <- dplyr::bind_cols(
  turtle_internesting,
  turtle_turbidity %>% dplyr::select(-ID)
)

# Check resulting dataset
dplyr::glimpse(turtle_turbidity)

# Summarise turbidity proxy values
summary(turtle_turbidity$Turbidity_Proxy)

# Count observations without turbidity data
sum(is.na(turtle_turbidity$Turbidity_Proxy))
```

### 3.5.5 Import inter-nesting tracking observations

```{r turtle-turbidity-overlay-inter-nesting, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
# Import inter-nesting tracking observations
turtle_internesting <- readr::read_csv(
  here::here("outputs", "Turtle_Internesting_Cleaned.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Convert turtle coordinates into spatial points
turtle_points <- terra::vect(
  turtle_internesting,
  geom = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)

# Match the coordinate system of the turbidity raster
turtle_points <- terra::project(
  turtle_points,
  terra::crs(turbidity)
)

# Plot turbidity
plot(
  turbidity,
  main = "Inter-nesting Turtle Locations and Water Turbidity (2024)",
  col = hcl.colors(100, "Viridis"),
  range = c(0, 0.1227)
)

points(
  turtle_points,

  cex = 0.35

```
```{r turbidity-dot-distribution, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
# Calculate median turbidity
median_turbidity <- median(
  turtle_turbidity$Turbidity_Proxy,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
# Calculate the density curve and identify its two highest peaks
density_data <- density(
  turtle_turbidity$Turbidity_Proxy,
  na.rm = TRUE,
  adjust = 1
)

# Find local peaks in the density curve
peak_indices <- which(
  diff(sign(diff(density_data$y))) == -2
) + 1

# Select the two highest peaks
peak_indices <- peak_indices[
  order(density_data$y[peak_indices], decreasing = TRUE)
]

peak_indices <- head(peak_indices, 2)

# Create labels with turbidity values and nearby observation counts
peak_labels <- tibble(
  turbidity = density_data$x[peak_indices],
  density = density_data$y[peak_indices]
) %>%
  mutate(
    observations = sapply(turbidity, function(x) {
      sum(abs(turtle_turbidity$Turbidity_Proxy - x) <= 0.005,
          na.rm = TRUE)
    }),
    label = paste0(
      "Turbidity: ", round(turbidity, 3),
      "\nObservations: ", observations
    ),
    y_position = density / max(density_data$y) * 0.8 + 0.1
  )

# Display tracking observations and their density distribution
ggplot(turtle_turbidity, aes(x = Turbidity_Proxy)) +
geom_jitter(
  aes(y = 0.5),
  height = 0.45,
  width = 0,
  colour = "#70A88B",
  alpha = 0.3,
  size = 1.3
) +
  geom_density(
  aes(y = after_stat(scaled) * 0.8 + 0.1),
  colour = "#326B49",
  linewidth = 1.2,
  fill = NA,
  adjust = 1
) +
  geom_label(
  data = peak_labels,
  aes(
    x = turbidity,
    y = y_position,
    label = label
  ),
  inherit.aes = FALSE,
  size = 3,
  fill = "white",
  colour = "#326B49",
  label.size = 0.2,
  vjust = -0.3
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = median_turbidity,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "#326B49",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Inter-nesting Turtle Observations Across Turbidity Gradients",
    subtitle = "Dots represent tracking observations; curve shows relative concentration",
    x = "Turbidity Proxy (2024)",
    y = "Relative Concentration of Observations"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank()
  )
```

### 3.5.8 Turtle Tracking Locations Coloured by Turbidity

```{r mangrove-turbidity-overlay, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# Extract turbidity values for inter-nesting turtle locations
turtle_points_turbidity <- terra::vect(
  turtle_internesting,
  geom = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)

turtle_points_turbidity <- terra::project(
  turtle_points_turbidity,
  terra::crs(turbidity)
)

Turbidity_Proxys <- terra::extract(
  turbidity,
  turtle_points_turbidity
)

# Combine tracking observations with extracted turbidity
turtle_mangrove_turbidity <- dplyr::bind_cols(
  turtle_internesting,
  Turbidity_Proxys %>% dplyr::select(-ID)
)

# Convert to spatial points in the mangrove projection
turtle_turbidity_map <- terra::vect(
  turtle_mangrove_turbidity,
  geom = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)

turtle_turbidity_map <- terra::project(
  turtle_turbidity_map,
  "EPSG:7856"
)

# Use the same Viridis colour scale as the ridgeline plot
turbidity_palette <- hcl.colors(100, "Viridis")

turbidity_limits <- range(
  turtle_mangrove_turbidity$Turbidity_Proxy,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

turbidity_index <- round(
  (turtle_mangrove_turbidity$Turbidity_Proxy -
     turbidity_limits[1]) /
    diff(turbidity_limits) * 99
) + 1

turbidity_index <- pmax(1, pmin(100, turbidity_index))

point_colours <- turbidity_palette[turbidity_index]

# Plot mangrove buffers
plot(
  mangrove_buffer_1km,
  col = "#F0E8CF",
  border = NA,
  main = "Turtle Turbidity Conditions Near Mangroves",
  axes = FALSE,
  box = FALSE
)

plot(mangrove_buffer_500m,
     col = "#B9D8B0", border = NA, add = TRUE)

plot(mangrove_buffer_100m,
     col = "#72A77A", border = NA, add = TRUE)

plot(mangrove_polygons,
     col = "#326B49", border = NA, add = TRUE)

# Overlay turtle locations coloured by turbidity
points(
  turtle_turbidity_map,
  pch = 16,
  col = adjustcolor(point_colours, alpha.f = 0.75),
  cex = 0.55
)
# Leave additional space below the map
par(mar = c(8, 2, 3, 5), xpd = NA)

# Draw mangrove legend below the map
```
